purpose:

(Proposed Submission Version) to Council and seek approval that it
can be published for public representation under Regulation 19 for

content:
To present the Local Plan
(Proposed Submission Version) to Council and seek approval that it
can be published for public representation under Regulation 19 for
a period of 6 weeks.

(Key
Decision):
 
Cabinet is asked to Recommend to Full Council that
it:
 
1)   
Agrees the Proposed Submission Local Plan
(Regulation 19) (Report Appendix 1), and the Proposed
Submission Policies Map (Report Appendix 2) for public
consultation.

 
2)   
Notes that supporting documents to be published
alongside the Proposed Submission Local Plan Appendix 1 (Local Plan
consultation document) and Report Appendix 2 (Policies Map) for the
consultation include:

 
a.   
Statement of Consultation (Regulation 18) (including
summaries of representations received)
b.   
Sustainability Appraisal (including the Sustainable
Environmental Assessment)
c.    
Habitats Regulations Assessment
d.   
Infrastructure Delivery Plan
e.   
Thematic Topic Papers
f.     
Equality and Fairness Appraisal
g.   
Suite of other Evidence Studies as identified in
paragraph 2.45 in this report.

 
3)   
Agrees that any subsequent material amendments to be
made to the Local Plan (Report Appendices 1 and 2) prior to
consultation will be approved by the Cabinet Member for Regulatory
Services, Staff and Performance, Enterprise.

 
4)   
Agrees to delegate authority to the Chief Executive
(and the Head of Planning Policy), in consultation with the Cabinet
Member for Regulatory Services, Staff and Performance, Enterprise,
to make any necessary editorial changes and/or minor amendments
that do not materially affect the content (where necessary) prior
to publication for consultation.

 
5)   
Notes that public consultation, if approved, will be
for a period of six weeks, as stated in the Statement of Community
Involvement.

report.

30 new affordable homes – Appendix 2 (exempt) to the
report.

allocation within the Housing Revenue Account (HRA) Capital

emergency accommodation (EA).

Housing, Assets and Development, in consultation with the Director
of Finance and Performance (S151 Officer) and Cabinet Member for
Housing and Homelessness, to progress the recommendations including
the approval of business cases, implementation of all processes and
procedures, allocation of budgets, negotiation and agreement of
terms and lease agreements, award of contract(s), and authorising
the execution of all related documentation including grant funding
agreements.

content:
To seek Cabinet approval for
the adoption of the Eastbourne Seafront Strategy 2050, which sets
out a long-term vision and strategic framework for the regeneration
of Eastbourne’s seafront through to 2050. The strategy aligns
with the Pevensey to Eastbourne Coastal Management Plan and
responds to extensive public consultation, setting out priorities
across heritage, culture, tourism, health and leisure, and
inclusive access.
 

To approve the
Eastbourne Seafront Strategy 2050 as the guiding framework for
future seafront regeneration and investment.
To endorse the phased
Deliverables Plan, recognising it will evolve over time in response
to funding opportunities, stakeholder input, and project
development.
To delegate authority
to officers to progress Phase 1 deliverables, including funding
bids, feasibility work, and stakeholder engagement.
To establish the
Seafront Programming Working Group to oversee delivery, governance,
and community engagement.



(Key decision):
1)   
To approve the Eastbourne Seafront Strategy 2050
enclosed within Report Appendix 1 as the guiding framework for
future seafront regeneration and investment.
2)   
To endorse the phased Deliverables Plan enclosed
within Report Appendix 2, recognising it will evolve over time in
response to funding opportunities, stakeholder input, and project
development.
3) 
To establish the Seafront Executive Board to support
delivery, programming, governance, and community engagement and
approve the early establishment of a Bandstand Task Force to
oversee restoration, funding strategy, and engagement with the
Environment Agency.
4)

Regeneration and Planning, in consultation with the Leader of the
Council and also the Cabinet Member for
Heritage, Culture and Seafront, to progress
all phase 1 deliverables of the Strategy, including feasibility
work, and stakeholder engagement, and making funding bids for
opportunities including National Lottery Heritage Fund, Arts
Council England, and other relevant sources.

purpose:
To seek approval of the Leader
of the Council for the Council to apply for living wage
accreditation and become a Real Living Wage employer.
content:
To seek approval of the Leader
of the Council for the Council to apply for living wage
accreditation and become a Real Living Wage employer.

To delegate authority to the
Director of Finance and Performance to apply for Eastbourne Borough
Council to become a Living Wage employer and commit to paying Real
Living Wage to all staff.

This would enable the Council
to play more of an advocacy role in encouraging other local
employers to pay the Real Living Wage to staff, raising standards
of living for people working in the region.

Not applying for the living
wage would save money but not contribute to raising standards of
living of staff and would not enable the Council to play an
advocacy role for Real Living Wage in the town.
topline: The Leader of Eastbourne Borough Council has decided to apply for living wage accreditation and commit to paying the Real Living Wage to all staff.
